steps.content: You step out of Compartment 104 and nearly crash right into the train attendant. Allison jumps, startled, and stumbles to a halt.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Perfect timing, Allison. I was just looking for you.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: What's your take on this tragedy?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: That's right. I'd like to hear your thoughts. I'm trying to get a different perspective on things.
You pull out your notebook and begin taking notes.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Um... The doctor said Ms. Clementine had twelve stab wounds to her chest, but only the first few were fatal. The rest were just... frenzied stabbing. Like someone venting their rage.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: But the compartment window was left open. Maybe the killer jumped out after committing the murder?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Anything else? Like the note that was left at the crime scene, for instance. It mentioned an interesting phrase—"The Burning Redwood." Have you heard of it?

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: I think... it was a fire from a long time ago? I was still young back then, though, so I don't really know the details.
Allison rubs her chin, trying to recall the incident, but ultimately can't provide much information. She's apologetic that she couldn't be of more help.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: That's all right. What you've given me is enough. There's just one more thing I need your help with.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: All the passengers who entered the first-class carriage that night have been gathered in the dining car. I need you to relay a message to them. Once I give you the signal, bring them back to their compartments one by one—

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: I'd like to ask them all something.
